data.heading: The circulatory system
The heart
data.text: The circulatory system is a combination of the heart, blood, and blood vessels. It transports blood, oxygen, and nutrients throughout the body and carries away waste products.
The arteries carry blood away from the heart to other organs and tissues in the body.
The veins carry blood without oxygen from other parts of the body to the heart.
The capillaries are very small blood vessels that link veins to arteries.
The two upper chambers of the heart are known as atriums.
The two lower chambers of the heart are known as ventricles.
The right side and the left side of the heart are separated by a wall called septum.
The blood from different parts of the body enters the right atrium and is then pushed into the right ventricle.
Blood from the right ventricle enters the lungs where it receives oxygen.
Oxygen-rich blood enters the left atrium and then the left ventricle.
The oxygen-rich blood travels around the body through arteries to provide cells with oxygen and other nutrients.
